quest.title: Smokeless War
quest.description: You've finally found some key materials. All that's left is to cook the mushroom and see what happens...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Primogem x60, Mora x44000, Guide to Conflict x5, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Return to the tribe and prepare to cook the mushrooms

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back! And we found a bunch of stuff to use!

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Great! We're almost done with the preparations on our side, too.

dialogues.speaker: Atolli
dialogues.text: I've managed to get these iron chunks red-hot. We should be good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yeah, and since we need really high temperatures, I brought the best stove I could find!

dialogues.speaker: Xoctli
dialogues.text: And I've got a bunch of buckets of lava on standby if we need more fuel, hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's like we're gearing up for a fight, not cooking a few mushrooms...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but the things we brought aren't your typical cooking utensils either...

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Well, that mushroom started it, right everyone? Disrespecting Varesa and our guest of honor...

dialogues.speaker: Camotli
dialogues.text: Yeah! We'll see what sort of excuses it can come up with this time!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Thanks for the help, everyone. It really means a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Atolli
dialogues.text: Alright, let's see what we have here... Huh? The armor of a Furnace Shell Mountain Weasel? Don't tell me, you went into the volcano!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No no, it erupted out of nowhere, and the weasel appeared, and then... Well, anyway, we got this in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Atolli
dialogues.text: Either way, this is something special. Back when I was training to be a chef, I studied the effect of temperature on different ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Atolli
dialogues.text: This kind of armor produces intense localized heat. It's great for fish because you can get a nice sear on one side without overcooking the other.

dialogues.speaker: Atolli
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's get started! The mushrooms are all ready to go.

dialogues.speaker: Xoctli
dialogues.text: Alright, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, the fragrance is so much more intense... And, what's with this weird mist?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no... Something's not right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where are we? Where did everyone go!?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I have no idea. We just showed up here... I can't see the others anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Huh? Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That's Acatl... Chief! We don't know where we are!

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: What? I know it's hard to see through this mist, but aren't you here at the tribe with the rest of us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you didn't feel anything strange?

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: No... What are you feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This must be the Sage-Lord's trick, but it's only affecting the three of us.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But... Why us and not the others?)

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Because you are the only worthy devotees, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Evil jerk of a mushroom! So, this is what you look like!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Huh... He does look a bit more evil than the other mushrooms we met.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: I am no longer concerned with your insolence. On the contrary, I am satisfied with your performance. So, as promised, you shall have the answers you seek.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Of course, I have a goal of my own. Let me reiterate once more: the great Sage-Lord of Fungi — that would be me — is extending you the honor of becoming my subjects.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, the only way anyone's serving you is on a platter!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Now, now, don't be hasty. It's inadvisable to speak in absolutes. You refuse only because you have yet to witness my miracles.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Cherish this opportunity. It may not come again.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: As you know, Teyvat is not a peaceful place. The gods wage war against one another, monsters roam the land, humans live in squalor...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: But, then, humanity discovered me and learned that I could grant them unlimited power to fell even the most fearsome of enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Soletl
dialogues.text: If we wanna become strong, we just have to eat this!

dialogues.speaker: Teoxoletl
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Teoxoletl
dialogues.text: Those monsters are no match for me!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: And, so, the humans worshiped me as their savior, and in return, I revealed my identity as the Sage-Lord of Fungi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really expect us to believe that? Besides... As far as enemies go, a few puny Fungi aren't all that "fearsome"...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Such arrogance! Take that back and apologize before I lose my temper!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, you wish!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I mean, those monsters really don't look that scary — not the kind you need a "miracle" to defeat, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: You insignificant mortals boast of strength? Very well, then prove it!

talks.objective: Talk to the Sage-Lord of Fungi

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: W—Well fought. You see? You ate a fair amount of my clones, and now look what you can do! Hmph, my eye for subjects is as discerning as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, weren't we "insignificant mortals" just a second ago? Weird...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: I'll admit, you're not entirely useless, but my miracles are even greater than you can imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, don't just— Ugh, another cryptic one-liner and another disappearing act. It's gotta be a mushroom thing at this point...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, what should we do? Follow him?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's go. I think he's trying to tell us a story, although I'm not sure if I like the plot...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: I soon became humanity's faith and, with my power, created countless clones with which I could bestow upon them an endless source of sustenance.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Food is a scarce resource. A faith that provides for the needs of the flesh is the most practical and noble of all!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: And as my subjects gave themselves in service, either as civilians or warriors, I rewarded them with mushrooms in proportion to their contribution. The most exceptional among them could receive as many as twenty mushrooms a day!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's it?

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: What are you insinuating? Are mushrooms not enough?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Well, it's possible people couldn't afford to be picky back then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but now, even saurians have more options than that...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Sustenance and strength... Such are the pillars of faith. So, what do you think? A pretty enticing offer, wouldn't you agree?

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Once you become my subjects, all you have to do is build a civilization dedicated to the mushrooms, and then—

choices.text: Hold on...

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: What do you mean, "what happened next"?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Right! If the humans dedicated themselves in service to you, then shouldn't you have your own tribe at this point? Or even your own nation?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: But, I've read a lot of woven scrolls about the heroes of Natlan, and I've never come across anything about some kind of mushroom savior.

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: Of course not! I was in a different nation at the time. I don't suppose you know their history, too...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've been to Sumeru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! And we didn't hear anything about a mushroom civilization.

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: I never said it was Sumeru! I have no idea where that assumption is coming from...

choices.text: Because Fungi are creatures from Sumeru.

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: A... A trivial detail! You know what? You don't deserve to know what happened next!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then you don't deserve our faith, either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! If you want us to respect you, stop being so secretive!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: True, if we don't know how the story ends, it doesn't hold much weight, now does it...

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: *frustrated grumble*

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: Alright, fine. Same rules as before — if you want the truth, you'll have to use your wits to earn it!

response.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
response.text: If you fail to prove your worth, good luck getting another detail out of me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, he ran off! C'mon, after him!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Oh, uh-huh... Right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He jumped down from here! So, it looks like we just need to—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hold on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Something wrong, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's something off about his motive.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Off... how?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: That's how I feel, too... Based on his personality, if he won't tell us how things turned out in the end, it must be because it's not something he can brag about.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Besides, how did he even get from Sumeru to Natlan? Seems like he's avoiding that subject, too...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: And, through it all, he still hasn't given up on recruiting us... Even though he's in for a rude awakening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... He seemed pretty annoyed with our questions. Why not just kick us to the curb?

choices.text: He must be in dire need of subjects.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: But... why?

choices.text: Let's go after him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, sounds like a plan! Let's go!

choices.text: And keep an eye out for clues along the way.
And it has to be the three of us.
The buildings from your visions support that, too.
I want to know what happened next.

talks.objective: Catch up to the Sage-Lord of Fungi
Continue to pursue the Sage-Lord of Fungi
Continue to pursue the Sage-Lord of Fungi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xamaran!?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Y—You know that name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon calls it "Sheeshroom"... It's absolutely huge! Way more impressive than the puny Sage-Lord.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It took a long time for Xamaran to grow into this form. Luckily, Xamaran isn't a green-cap mushroom so there's no danger to us.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And, I believe its mind has been separated from the mushroom god for a very long time. I doubt there's a connection between them anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should go see Xamaran one of these days!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Ooh, I'll come! It'll be nice to interact with a friendly mushroom for once!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hehe, "friendly" is right, so this one is definitely not for eating!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I would never!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Backed into a corner, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: We've got you this time!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Oooow!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: That hurt, you know!? You humans have such violent tendencies!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did we lose him!?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: *sigh* Not again... Although, I think I pulled something off of him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, a ball... of mist? Oh no, it's spreading!

dialogues.speaker: Mushriwaili
dialogues.text: They're gonna eat us...

dialogues.speaker: Mushrial
dialogues.text: Gonna eat us...

dialogues.speaker: Mushriu
dialogues.text: Eat us...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Ungrateful humans...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: At this rate, I won't have any clones left...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: The more my clones are consumed... The less power I have... The situation grows dire.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Why must the humans eat so much!?

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Phew, my power is all but spent, but it was still enough to control a single human, at least...

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Now, all of Sumeru knows how scrumptious my mushrooms are, so if I want to grow... I must relocate.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: And, if I want it to happen fast, I need suitable environmental conditions.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: You! Take me somewhere hot! The hotter, the better!

dialogues.speaker: Chatraka
dialogues.text: Yes, my lord!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Is this the place, human?

dialogues.speaker: Chatraka
dialogues.text: Yes, this is a volcano in a land far to the west. The temperatures here get very high. It should be a most suitable location for your lordship to regain his strength.

dialogues.speaker: Chatraka
dialogues.text: I shall now find a good place to plant you, my lord, so that your mycelial majesty may take root in this fertile land.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Yes, proceed.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Huh? An earthquake?

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: No, a volcanic eruption!? Aaaargh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that's how it ended. No wonder he tried to hide it from us, that's... pretty embarrassing.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I thought he said people formed communities around this mushroom and used it as their main source of food...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but it looks like his following got too big, and he couldn't keep up with the demand.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Huh, he used the mushrooms as his main recruitment tactic, but then the situation got out of control...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And, it seems like his power is proportional to the number of clones he has.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Which means, the more mushrooms the humans ate, the less powerful he became, right?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Wow, so his following didn't last long.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, which explains why there aren't any records about some kind of mushroom civilization.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In the end, he mind-controlled a human to bring him to Natlan and then got buried under a pile of volcanic rocks...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Yeah... For who knows how long...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: When we were talking to him earlier, he seemed kind of... out of touch, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, he has been living under a rock, so... that checks out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, clearing out this area for your orchard finally allowed him to start regaining his power.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Yeah, that sounds right. My parents always thought it was so weird that mushrooms kept popping up around the orchard no matter what we did... Now it makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Wait, but... If everything we saw is true, that means this mushroom has mind control powers or something? That's a recipe for disaster.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on, do you remember what he showed us? A group of humans worshipping a giant mushroom... It just doesn't make sense! They must have been mind-controlled!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, when he started running out of power, he couldn't keep it up!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! Maybe that's why he doesn't seem to be able to control us, either.

choices.text: I understand now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Why?

choices.text: I'll explain on the way.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Alright, then let's find this mushroom!

choices.text: I need to catch him to confirm my theory.
Why it has to be us.

talks.objective: Continue to pursue the Sage-Lord of Fungi
Continue to pursue the Sage-Lord of Fungi
Continue to pursue the Sage-Lord of Fungi
Talk to the Sage-Lord of Fungi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've got you this time, nasty mushroom! We know all your schemes!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe try hiding them a bit better next time.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: We thought you were just a mushroom that happened to taste good. But, now we know how dangerous you are, so we have to stop you!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Hm, it would seem you're not completely devoid of intelligence — fitting for my future subjects. Still, you're overlooking a very important detail.

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Did you think I was running away because I was scared? This is a world of my creation. My will rules supreme!

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: My "schemes" have been exposed you say? No matter. My goal has already been achieved.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Sage-Lord of Fungi
dialogues.text: Hmph, although I prefer to call myself the Sage-Lord of Fungi, in the human tongue, I am known by another name.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: You now behold the god, Bifrons! The sole protagonist in this endless carnage!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you're a god.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Indeed! Foolish, shallow, and ungrateful humans, have you forgotten your savior during this time of war? I am the god who's protecting countless of your kind during this Archon War!

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: You have no food with which to satiate your hunger, no means with which to counter the hordes of monsters. And the gods loom overhead, capable of reducing you to ashes with a simple snap of their fingers.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Just one word, and you could have had my protection. But, now, that opportunity is lost forever, and you only have your own stupidity and arrogance to blame!

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: No matter. My plan has already succeeded.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: What you saw when you cooked the mushrooms was not mist, but spores... set to sprout into green mushrooms very soon.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: And that's where their true power lies... Because, given a bit of time to grow, green mushrooms will multiply exponentially.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: You see, considering my current level of power, I had no way to create a large number of clones... Unless, of course, I had access to a source of extreme heat.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: And you delivered one to me on a silver platter! That was my plan all along.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you kept running away from us because... you needed to buy time?

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Precisely. Before long, the green mushrooms will multiply at an unstoppable rate, allowing me to return to the peak of my power.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Then, I shall reclaim my dignity and status as a god, achieve victory in the Archon War, and take revenge on Sumeru!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You have no concept of time, do you... News flash, the Archon War is old news, buddy.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Nonsense! Is that not the source of your suffering?

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: All I hear in this land is "war" this and "war" that. If you fear the Archon War, all the more reason to cower behind the protection of a god!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pretty sure they're talking about the war against the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: The Archon War... I guess I've heard about that once or twice, but only from outlanders.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Hah! I see what's going on here. You're using lies and trickery to befuddle me!

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: You know, my original plan was to imprison you here until the end of time, but now, I have a better idea...

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Once nothing is left of this land but an endless field of mushrooms, I'll set you free — you get the honor of witnessing that despair in person.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: Now, I was going to offer you a glimmer of hope by allowing you to pledge yourselves to me and take on the burden of managing my kingdom...

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: But now, the deal is off!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was an empty deal from the start.

dialogues.speaker: Bifrons
dialogues.text: What did you say?

choices.text: We weren't chosen because you saw something in us.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: The Traveler explained everything. The only reason I could hear you is because I've eaten so many mushrooms over the years.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and Paimon ate a whole bunch during the competition! Paimon's small, so it didn't take as many mushrooms for her to be affected!

choices.text: And I happen to have a special constitution.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Point being, most people would have to eat a monstrous amount of mushrooms to even hear you over the buzz of a mosquito!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, you latched onto us, a group of people who could actually hear your voice. In other words...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're too weak.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: You said your mushrooms need time to grow. Which means... You don't have enough power to keep us here.

response.speaker: Bifrons
response.text: I may not have my former strength, but keeping a few humans right where I want them is a small task. Unless you think you can take on a creature as vicious and powerful as the Jadeplume Terrorshroom!?

response.speaker: Bifrons
response.text: Because you definitely can't... right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Forget about him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's get out of here.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Yeah, if he was telling the truth, we need to get back to the tribe as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Bifrons
response.text: No, no, no, you must be bluffing. A few measly humans couldn't possibly be that powerful... And what's this about a war against the Abyss? Hey! I want answers!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Paimon's not gonna waste one more word on this guy. Let's go.

choices.text: Which made it easy to hear your voice.
We were your only option.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After hearing your story, Katheryne heads to the Speaker's Chamber to check if there are any scholars in the area...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Katheryne's back! And... isn't that Tighnari!?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Word from the Speaker's Chamber was that an Amurta scholar happened to be conducting research in the area. So, they helped me to get in touch.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's been a while, you two. So, you're the ones looking into the Sage-Lord of Fungi...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! You're an expert, so you must know all about him, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Of course. To those in the Amurta darshan, his case is a well-known part of ecological history.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: His power is tied to his number of clones, so at one point, he possessed a truly fearsome form. But, as his clones diminished in number, he got smaller and smaller, until he couldn't hold onto physical form at all.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And so, he became impossible to track. Scholars could only keep tabs on him by monitoring what remains of his clones. Now, I'm learning his true form fled to Natlan...?

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Yeah, the mushrooms started popping up in our orchard not too long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, from what I've heard, he has very few clones right now, so there's nothing to worry about. Feel free to use the mushrooms as you see fit — they really are delicious.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Of course, in the interest of research, I would prefer to send a few scholars from my darshan to monitor the situation every so often. What do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I wanted to get your permission before submitting a formal request to the Speaker's Chamber.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Of course! You're welcome any time, hehe. That's a huge help, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I wanted to ask, though... You said "what remains of his clones"... Does that mean there are clones outside of Natlan? Even now?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, yes. There's a huge one beneath The Chasm.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Ahhhhhh~ What a great meal! Thanks, everyone! I feel like a whole new me!

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: And, with that, we took care of all the green mushrooms!

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Now, care to tell me what happened earlier? It was lights out for all three of you...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell the chief everything that happened.

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Someone... planted a god in Varesa's orchard, and she's been eating it ever since?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. We know not every god that's still around is super strong, but this one reached a whole new low.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't imagine the bar getting any lower than that.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Also, didn't he have his facts all wrong? He kept going on about some kind of... "Archon War"?

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Ah, well... Natlan was never part of the Archon War, so it rarely comes up around these parts. It makes sense that you don't know much about it, Varesa.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, hold on! Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Of course! The in-fighting between the dragons pretty much took over everything, so there was no room for the gods to join in.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that checks out. Living under a rock all those years, mushroom-god wakes up, thinking it's still the Archon War and tries to use that to convince people to worship him...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Hehe, little did he know, our lives are much better now than in the age of the dragons!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do we do now? It can't be easy to slay a god...

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I guess it's back to business as usual. As long as we keep picking the green mushrooms, that god is just a tasty mushroom at the end of the day.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: #Actually, um, {NICKNAME}... Can I borrow you for a minute?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Alright, here's good. So, um, it's not anything super important. I just wanted to thank you... from the bottom of my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Your encouragement gave me the courage to investigate the green mushrooms and helped me resolve a threat to my tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: And, maybe this sounds weird, considering everything... But, it was a really awesome adventure! I had fun!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Me too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's an adventure I'll remember for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Oh? Why's that?

choices.text: You got the chance to shine as a hero.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: You're right!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: I never thought my appetite would save the day... It's pretty surreal.

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: But, it's like you said — all it takes is a little patience and perseverance, and my time will come!

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: If I start to doubt myself in the future, all I need to do is think of this experience and everything I've learned along the way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yep! You got this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you two!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Acatl was saying that, since a scholar from Sumeru warned the tribe about the mushrooms, someone there must know about the mushroom god.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should we go check it out? Couldn't hurt to get more information...

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Oh, good point! But, if we're heading to the Akademiya, I need to get permission from Uncle Acatl first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, and it's not a quick trip. We have to cross the whole desert.

choices.text: Why don't we just ask the Adventurers' Guild?

response.speaker: Varesa
response.text: Good idea! Let's check it out!

choices.text: Who knows, maybe there's a Sumeru scholar in Natlan right now.
And it was all you, through and through.

talks.objective: Head to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame to seek help

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Xamaran is its name. Its mycelium structure is stunning, and it's capable of human speech.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that sounds amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It took a long time for Xamaran to grow into this form. Luckily, Xamaran isn't a green-cap mushroom so there's no danger to us.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And, I believe its mind has been separated from the mushroom god for a very long time. I doubt there's a connection between them anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should go see Xamaran one of these days!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: Ooh, I'll come! It'll be nice to interact with a friendly mushroom for once!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hehe, "friendly" is right, so this one is definitely not for eating!

dialogues.speaker: Varesa
dialogues.text: I would never!

dialogues.speaker: Atolli
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's get started! The mushrooms are all ready to go.

dialogues.speaker: Xoctli
dialogues.text: Alright, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, the fragrance is so much more intense... And, what's with this weird mist?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no... Something's not right...
